text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that can understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users can improve results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are good at tasks like answering questions, summarising texts and writing emails. However, they also have limits. They sometimes produce incorrect information, cannot truly understand meaning, and may reflect biases found in their training data. For these reasons, people should always check important information carefully.
